charging-station.definition: A place or piece of equipment where an electric vehicle can connect to receive electrical energy.
charging-station.exampleUsage: The car stopped at a charging station during the trip.

plug.definition: A small object that fits into a socket to connect an appliance to electricity.

cable.definition: A conductor for transmitting electrical or optical signals or electric power.

adapter.definition: A device that lets equipment with different connectors work together.

level-1.definition: To level a surface is to flatten it by removing bumps and uneven parts.

level-2.definition: To level a surface is to flatten it by removing bumps and uneven parts.

dc-fast-charger.definition: A high-power charger that supplies direct current to an electric vehicle battery for relatively rapid charging.
dc-fast-charger.exampleUsage: The display showed the DC fast charger's current status.

charging-port.definition: The socket or connection point on a vehicle where a charging cable is attached.
charging-port.exampleUsage: The driver opened the charging port before connecting the cable.

payment-terminal.definition: An electronic device used to accept and process payments.
payment-terminal.exampleUsage: The payment terminal displayed the session cost.

battery-pack.definition: A group of battery cells and related components assembled together to store electrical energy.
battery-pack.exampleUsage: The vehicle's battery pack is mounted beneath the floor.

electric-motor.definition: A machine that converts electrical energy into rotational motion, usually by using coils and magnets to create a turning force.

regenerative-braking.definition: A braking system in electric and hybrid vehicles that changes some energy from motion into electricity and stores it in the battery.

inverter.definition: An electrical converter that converts direct current into alternating current.

onboard-charger.definition: A charger built into an electric vehicle that converts incoming AC electricity into a form the battery can store.
onboard-charger.exampleUsage: The onboard charger manages AC charging inside the vehicle.

thermal-management.definition: A system for controlling the temperature of batteries, motors, or other components so they operate within a suitable range.
thermal-management.exampleUsage: The thermal-management system helps control battery temperature.

drive-unit.definition: The group of components that produces and transfers power to move an electric vehicle, often including an electric motor and gearing.
drive-unit.exampleUsage: The drive unit sends power to the wheels.

power-electronics.definition: Electronic components that control, convert, and distribute electrical power in a vehicle or energy system.
power-electronics.exampleUsage: Power electronics manage energy between the battery and motor.

bms.definition: Solid excretory product evacuated from the bowels.

cell.definition: (biology) the basic structural and functional unit of all organisms.

parking-spot.definition: A marked space where a vehicle may be parked.
parking-spot.exampleUsage: The charging cable reaches the marked parking spot.

solar-panel.definition: A device with linked semiconductor cells that changes sunlight directly into electrical power.

signage.definition: Signs collectively (especially commercial signs or posters).

bollard.definition: A strong post (as on a wharf or quay or ship for attaching mooring lines).

curb.definition: A stock exchange in New York, previously known as the New York Curb Exchange.

handicap-space.definition: A parking space reserved for vehicles used by people with disabilities who meet local eligibility rules.
handicap-space.exampleUsage: The accessible parking space is kept clear for eligible users.

bench.definition: A level shelf of land interrupting a declivity (with steep slopes above and below).

rfid-card.definition: A card containing a radio-frequency identification chip that can be read wirelessly at short range.
rfid-card.exampleUsage: The RFID card identifies an authorized account at the station.

mobile-app.definition: A software program built to work on a smartphone or tablet, usually obtained through an app store or another digital platform.

qr-code.definition: A QR code uses a shared standard that defines its square pattern, information capacity, versions, and error correction, so different devices and apps can scan it reliably.

account.definition: A record or narrative description of past events.

subscription.definition: A payment for consecutive issues of a newspaper or magazine for a given period of time.

per-kwh.definition: Charged or measured according to each kilowatt-hour of electrical energy.
per-kwh.exampleUsage: The screen shows the energy price per kWh.

session-fee.definition: A fixed charge applied for starting or using a charging session, separate from any energy charge.
session-fee.exampleUsage: The receipt lists the session fee separately.

receipt.definition: An acknowledgment (usually tangible) that payment has been made.

network.definition: An interconnected system of things or people.

roaming.definition: An arrangement that lets a customer use charging stations from different networks through compatible accounts or services.
roaming.exampleUsage: Roaming can allow access across several charging networks.

kilowatt.definition: A unit of power equal to 1000 watts.

state-of-charge.definition: A device indicator shows the amount of electrical charge remaining in its battery.

range.definition: An area in which something acts or operates or has power or control:.

voltage.definition: The rate at which energy is drawn from a source that produces a flow of electricity in a circuit.

amperage.definition: The strength of an electrical current measured in amperes.

charging-speed.definition: The rate at which electrical energy is delivered to an electric vehicle battery.
charging-speed.exampleUsage: Charging speed can change as the battery fills.

time-remaining.definition: An estimate of how much time is left before a process or session is expected to finish.
time-remaining.exampleUsage: The screen displayed the estimated time remaining.

energy-used.definition: The amount of electrical energy consumed or transferred during a period or session.
energy-used.exampleUsage: The receipt shows the energy used during charging.

cost.definition: The total spent for goods or services including money and time and labor.

efficiency.definition: Skillfulness in avoiding wasted time and effort.

ground-fault.definition: An electrical fault in which current flows to ground along an unintended path.
ground-fault.exampleUsage: The charger stopped after detecting a ground fault.

emergency-stop.definition: Describes a device or control built to halt machinery at once during an emergency, reducing the risk of injury or damage.

ventilation.definition: A mechanical system in a building that provides fresh air.

firmware-update.definition: A manufacturer-provided software package changes the built-in instructions that control a hardware device. It may fix faults, close security gaps, or add new functions.

weatherproof.definition: Able to withstand exposure to weather without damage.

tamper-proof.definition: Designed to resist unauthorized opening, alteration, or interference.
tamper-proof.exampleUsage: The outdoor connector uses a tamper-proof cover.

lockout.definition: A management action resisting employee's demands.

certification.definition: The act of certifying or bestowing a franchise on.

warranty.definition: A written assurance that some product or service will be provided or will meet certain specifications.
